stimulus.text: A tank contains 20 liters of water. The water drains from the tank at a constant rate of 2 liters per minute. After \(x\) minutes, the amount of water remaining in the tank, in liters, is given by the expression \(20 - 2x\). The situation in which more than 14 liters of water remain in the tank is modeled by the inequality \(20 - 2x \gt 14\).

stem: Which of the following is the solution to the given inequality?
rationale: Isolate \(x\): subtracting 20 from both sides of \(20 - 2x \gt 14\) gives \(-2x \gt -6\). Dividing both sides by \(-2\) reverses the inequality symbol, yielding \(x \lt 3\). Two checks confirm this: the interior point \(x = 0\) gives \(20 \gt 14\), which is true, and the boundary point \(x = 3\) gives \(14 \gt 14\), which is false — so the boundary must be excluded and the strict symbol is correct. Choice C results from dividing \(-6\) by \(-2\) to get the correct boundary \(3\) but forgetting to reverse the inequality symbol when dividing by a negative. Choice B keeps the correct direction but swaps the strict symbol for an inclusive one, wrongly admitting the boundary value \(x = 3\), which leaves exactly 14 liters rather than more than 14. Choice A compounds both errors: it reverses neither the direction nor excludes the boundary, giving the inclusive ray pointing the wrong way.
